tests/e2e/integration/trash-undo.test.ts.method: Whole source read in contiguous ranges 1-230 and 231-234.

findings: Six scenarios cover baseline/multibatch UI trash, baseline/multibatch optimistic undo, immediate command failure and cancel confirmation. They use injected precomputed groups plus programmed GPTK stub.
Unlike live trash E2E, integration tests correctly click MUI confirmation button. This narrows prior missing-confirmation finding to the live test source.
Comment counts 3x101 items as 303 trash keys, but default one kept per group yields 300 selected trash keys, still two batches (250+50). No exact requested-key count assertion in these cases.
Test titled shows trashing state only awaits final snackbar/group disappearance; no assertion checks intermediate progress UI or batch values.
Undo assertions inspect restored groups only. No restore-failure override, delayed acknowledgement or partial restoration scenario establishes backend/UI agreement.
Cancel test asserts dialog/results state, not absence of command on stub/backend. It does not directly count outgoing calls.
Error scenario fails before any stub work; no successful first batch followed by later failure, account change or stale undo snapshot tested.
limits: Static test review, no browser launch or trash/restore actions.
71/84 tracked files completely reviewed; no production library changes.
